items.title: From theory to delivery: How Atos upskilled 400 engineers in agentic AI
items.summary: When Atos set out to upskill 400 engineers in agentic AI, hands-on learning was the missing ingredient. Over three days, engineers built multi-agent systems on AWS through an AI League event. This post explains why Atos chose the format, what engineers built and learned, and what other enterprises should consider.

items.title: Tokenomics at scale: How Jamf built real-time spend enforcement for Amazon Bedrock
items.summary: As generative AI adoption scales, cost governance becomes a top challenge. Learn how Jamf built real-time, per-user spend enforcement for Amazon Bedrock using IAM Customer Managed Policies, an Amazon Athena cost view, and a serverless AWS Lambda loop that applies tiered model limits in near-real-time without disrupting active sessions.

items.title: Securing Amazon Quick from POC to production: Agents, Flows, and Spaces
items.summary: Amazon Quick proof-of-concept projects often stall when security teams review the production plan. This post walks through designing dashboards, Spaces, knowledge bases, agents, and Flows with security controls that hold as you scale: dataset shaping, agent isolation, document classification, and approval gates.

items.title: How t54 built a trust layer with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments
items.summary: t54 built x402-secure, a trust layer on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments that scores every endpoint before an autonomous agent pays it. See how session budgets, credential isolation, and a deterministic trust gate have governed more than 20 million agent-initiated transactions with no human in the loop.

items.title: How ZS democratized secure ad-hoc analytics with Amazon SageMaker
items.summary: Learn how ZS built a security-hardened Amazon SageMaker platform that balances developer agility with healthcare-grade governance, serving 1,000+ daily active users across 200+ SageMaker domains.

items.title: How Boomi Scribe streamlines documentation using AWS
items.summary: Boomi Scribe is an AI-powered agent on AWS that automatically generates documentation for enterprise integration workflows. Learn how Boomi uses Amazon Bedrock, Amazon SageMaker AI, Amazon S3, Amazon DynamoDB, and AWS Lambda to parse integration DAGs, generate detailed documentation, and compare component versions at scale.

items.title: Connect an AgentCore Runtime hosted MCP server to Amazon Quick
items.summary: In this post, you will learn how to deploy and host your MCP server in AgentCore Runtime and integrate it with Amazon Quick, along with the prerequisites. With this pattern, you promote reusability and avoid duplication of AI tools, so clients can reuse commonly used tools and agents exposed through an MCP server instead of authoring them from scratch again. Your customers get a way to use your product inside Amazon Quick (chat agents and workflows) without building custom connectors for every use case.

items.title: AWS recognized as a Leader in The Forrester Wave: AI Infrastructure Solutions, Q4 2025
items.summary: We’re excited to share that AWS has been recognized as a Leader in The Forrester Wave: AI Infrastructure Solutions, Q4 2025. In this evaluation of 13 providers, AWS received the highest score in the Strategy category.

items.title: Manage agents, tools and skills at scale with AWS Agent Registry
items.summary: AWS Agent Registry is now generally available: a single, searchable, governed catalog for the agents, tools, skills, and custom resources across your organization. This post explains what Registry is and walks through its publishing, curation, and discovery workflows, plus enterprise considerations and what’s next.

items.title: Build observable enterprise agentic retrieval using Managed Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Base with AWS CloudFormation
items.summary: This post builds an enterprise agentic retrieval solution on the Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. An agent reasons, routes across multiple knowledge bases, and returns cited answers, with seven layers of observability and both on-demand and continuous evaluation, all deployed with a single AWS CloudFormation chain.
